name: How much does a tub-to-shower conversion cost in Los Angeles if plumbing has to move?

mainEntity.name: How much does a tub-to-shower conversion cost in Los Angeles if the drain, valve, or supply lines need to be relocated?
mainEntity.text: How much does a tub-to-shower conversion cost in Los Angeles if the drain, valve, or supply lines need to be relocated?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion gets more expensive when the existing plumbing does not line up with the new shower layout. The biggest cost drivers are drain relocation, valve replacement, wall repair, waterproofing, and any subfloor work needed to set the shower pan correctly. In many homes, especially older Los Angeles-area properties, hidden issues such as corroded pipes or water damage can add to the budget after demolition begins. Homeowners should ask for a line-item estimate that separates demolition, plumbing, waterproofing, tile or wall panels, glass, and finishing. That makes it easier to compare bids and understand what is included. If the goal is to control cost, keeping the new shower in the same footprint as the tub is usually the cheapest path. If accessibility is the reason for the remodel, it is often worth spending more on a safer layout, better drain placement, and durable waterproofing rather than choosing the lowest bid.
acceptedAnswer.description: If plumbing has to move, the price usually rises because the contractor must open walls or floors, reroute drain and supply lines, and then waterproof and finish the area. A straightforward swap costs less than a conversion that changes the drain location, adds a new shower valve, or requires framing repairs.
